complexity.correctness_reason: Both decode and encode recurse to depth proportional to the list length, so lists longer than CPython's recursion limit (~1000 frames, minus interpreter overhead) raise RecursionError — impossible under the stated 100-node cap but reachable once it is lifted.
complexity.notes: Correct but unidiomatic: the standard solution is a single iterative pass with a carry, avoiding both the intermediate big integers and recursion. The triple decode/encode traversal also does ~3x the work of the one-pass approach.
complexity.summary: Recursively decodes both lists into integers, adds them, and recursively re-encodes the sum as a linked list, special-casing zero.
